newsitem.title: USA: Oglethorpe says it, Morgan agree power deal.
newsitem.headline: Oglethorpe says it, Morgan agree power deal.

text.p: Oglethorpe Power Corp said Wednesday its board has authorized its president and chief executive officer to finalize an agreement with Morgan Stanley Capital Group for Morgan Stanley to supply up to half of Oglethorpe's long-term, system-wide power requirements.
"The contract is expected to have a term of up to eight years. Details are still being finalized," Oglethorpe said in a statement.

Atlanta-based Oglethorpe, a wholesale power cooperative representing 39 of Georgia's 42 customer-owned electric utilities, said each member system has one month to decide whether they wish to participate in the deal.
This is Oglethorpe's second major power marketing deal.

The first, negotiated in November and approved earlier this month by the Rural Utilities Service, calls for LG&E Power Marketing, a subsidiary of LG&E Energy, to provide wholesale power to Oglethorpe over the next 15 years.
The LG&E agreement covers about 200 million Megawatt hours of electricity, or approximately the other half of Oglethorpe's long-term wholesale power supply needs.
"The proposal from Morgan Stanley provides substantial savings," Oglethorpe president and chief executive officer Tom Kilgore said in a prepared statement.

"In combination with our previous power marketing deal, this arrangement offers long-term price certainty that will further enhance our position in a utility environment that is becoming increasingly competitive," Kilgore said.

Oglethorpe Power provides wholesale electricity to 39 of Georgia's 42 customer-owned Electric Membership Corporations (EMCs) and claims to be the nation's largest power supply cooperative in terms of assets, customers, and power sales.
Oglethorpe's members serve about 2.6 million customers.
